messages.subject: User defined function for vectors?
parts:
I'm trying to make user defined functions.  I did an easy toy example for normal distribution. I called it "dnorm1"(for real numbers) "dnorm2"(for vectors).

My code:

#######################################################
######### Way 3. Use user-defined function ############

toy_code3 <- '
  functions {
    real dnorm_log(real x, real mu, real sigma){
    return -square(x-mu)/(2*square(sigma));
    } 
  }

  data {
    int<lower=0> N; 
    vector[N] y; 
    vector[N] x; 
  }

  parameters {
    real eta; 
    real mu0; 
    real mu1;
    real<lower=0> sigmasq;
  }

  transformed parameters {
    real<lower=0> sigma;
    real beta0;
    real beta1;
    sigma <- sqrt(sigmasq);
    beta0 <- mu0 + 10 * eta ;
    beta1 <- mu1 + 2 * eta ;
  }

  model {
    mu0 ~ dnorm(1, 1);
    mu1 ~ dnorm(1, 1);
    eta ~ dnorm(0, 1);
    sigmasq ~ inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001); 
    y ~ normal(beta0 + beta1*x, sigma);   #  y, x are vectors so I used the pre-defined function "normal"
                                 #  In the next code I wanted to define a function for vectors but it didn't work well. 
  }
'

toy_fit3 <- stan(model_code = toy_code3, data = toy_dat, 
            iter = 1000, chains = 2)

print(toy_fit3)
plot(toy_fit3)

#  Elapsed Time: 1.524 seconds (Warm-up)
#                1.203 seconds (Sampling)
#                2.727 seconds (Total)

########## Yes! Got same result as using the "normal"  ###

#post-warmup draws per chain=500, total post-warmup draws=1000.

#mu1       0.78    0.02 0.20   0.37   0.64   0.79   0.92   1.15   120 1.02
#sigmasq   0.85    0.01 0.12   0.65   0.77   0.84   0.92   1.14   294 1.00
#sigma     0.92    0.00 0.06   0.81   0.88   0.92   0.96   1.07   295 1.00
#beta0     2.07    0.00 0.09   1.88   2.01   2.07   2.13   2.25   648 1.00
#beta1     1.00    0.00 0.00   1.00   1.00   1.00   1.00   1.01  1000 1.00
#lp__    -42.82    0.10 1.45 -46.07 -43.55 -42.48 -41.75 -41.02   230 1.00



#######################################################
######### Way 5. Play around user-defined function ############

toy_code4 <- '
  functions {
    vector dnorm2_log(vector x2, vector mu2, real sigma2) {
      return -(dot_self(x2-mu2))/(2*square(sigma2));
    } 
  }

  data {
    int<lower=0> N; 
    vector[N] y; 
    vector[N] x; 
  }

  parameters {
    real eta; 
    real mu0; 
    real mu1;
    real<lower=0> sigmasq;
  }

  transformed parameters {
    real<lower=0> sigma;
    real beta0;
    real beta1;
    vector[N] mu;
    sigma <- sqrt(sigmasq);
    beta0 <- mu0 + 10 * eta ;
    beta1 <- mu1 + 2 * eta ;
  }

  model {
    mu0 ~ normal(1, 1);
    mu1 ~ normal(1, 1);
    eta ~ normal(0, 1);
    sigmasq ~ inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001); 
    y ~ dnorm2(beta0 + beta1*x, sigma);
  }
'

toy_fit4 <- stan(model_code = toy_code4, data = toy_dat, 
            iter = 1000, chains = 2)



The user defined function "dnorm1" (for real numbers) work very well, but the one for vectors ("dnorm2") gives the error as follows:

LOCATION OF PARSING ERROR (line = 6, position = 3):

PARSED:


  functions {
    vector dnorm2_log(vector x2, vector mu2, real sigma2) {
      return -(dot_self(x2-mu2))/(2*square(sigma2));
    } 
  

EXPECTED: <eps> BUT FOUND: 

}


Can anybody tell me why?    How to define a user-defined function for vectors?   Can a user defined function work for both real numbers and vectors?


Thanks a lot!

Dora

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] User defined function for vectors?
parts:
Please, everyone, when sending us error reports, please include
information about at least

(a) which version of Stan you're using and on which platform, and

(b) *all* all of the model, and

(c) all of the output Stan produces, not just what you think is relevant.

Otherwise, we have (a) guess what you're running, (b) guess what is
parameter vs. data, and (c) re-run it ourselves to see the full error
messages. (b) wasn't a problem in this post, but (c) was.

In your case, the full output is:

----------------------
EXPECTATION FAILURE - DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:

Base type mismatch. Returned expression does not match return type
LHS type = vector; RHS type = real
Improper return in body of function.

LOCATION OF PARSING ERROR (line = 5, position = 1):

PARSED:

functions {
vector dnorm2_log(vector x2, vector mu2, real sigma2) {
return -(dot_self(x2-mu2))/(2*square(sigma2));
}


EXPECTED: <eps> BUT FOUND:

}

--------------------------

The part above what you posted indicates that you're trying to return
a real value when the function is declared to return a vector. The
model compiles if you make the function return type real instead of vector.

The underlying reason is that unlike R, Stan is typed. In particular,
we don't automatically promote reals to vectors (which one would
we promote to, vector or row_vector?).

Our built-in normal distribution will be faster than anything you
can write in the language because we've optimized the gradient calculations
as well as dropping normalizing constants where legal. So I'm hoping this
is just for practice as you wrote in the doc. It's a great idea to start
with something simple where you know what the answer should be, and then
move on to something more complicated.

- Bob
